title: A quasi-coherent ideal sheaf on an integral scheme is nonzero iff its stalk at the generic point is the whole function field
statement:
Let $Z$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] [def-pc-scheme] with generic point $\eta$ (the unique point whose closure is $Z$ [def-weil-irreducible-components]), and let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals [pqf-def-coherent]; regard its stalk $\mathcal I_\eta$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] as an ideal of $\mathcal O_{Z,\eta}$ (the stalk map of the inclusion $\mathcal I	o\mathcal O_Z$ is injective). Then $\mathcal O_{Z,\eta}$ is a field, and the following are equivalent: (a) $\mathcal I
eq0$; (b) $\mathcal I(U)
eq0$ for every nonempty affine open $U\subseteq Z$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; (c) $\mathcal I_\eta
eq0$; (d) $\mathcal I_\eta=\mathcal O_{Z,\eta}$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 01YL (label lemma-property-irreducible-higher-rank-cohomological, coherent.tex line 3307, proof lines 3351-3415): used without statement in 'r > 0 and I is nonzero because the support of G is equal to Z_0' and in the claims that Q', Q''' have support properly contained in Z_0 (a nonzero ideal I' contained in I, and I' = I'' cap I)

proof.text: Let $U\subseteq Z$ be a nonempty affine open and put $R=\mathcal O_Z(U)$. Since $Z$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], $R$ is a domain. The generic point $\eta$ belongs to every nonempty open of the irreducible space $Z$: its closure is all of $Z$, so a nonempty open disjoint from $\eta$ would have a closed complement containing that closure. Under the canonical identification $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points], $\eta$ corresponds to $(0)$, the generic point of the spectrum of the domain $R$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field](2). That lemma identifies $\mathcal O_{Z,\eta}$ with the fraction field of $R$; in particular it is a field.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 01YL, label lemma-property-irreducible-higher-rank-cohomological, third paragraph; the generic-point calculation is supplied from Properties Lemma 01ON and Schemes Lemma 01HV

proof.text: For every nonempty affine open $U$ as in step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-zero-set-affine] applied to $\mathcal I$ at the prime $(0)$ says $\mathcal I_\eta=\mathcal O_{Z,\eta}$ exactly when $\mathcal I(U)\not\subseteq(0)$, equivalently $\mathcal I(U)\ne0$. Hence (d) implies (b), while (b) implies (d) by choosing any nonempty affine open of the nonempty scheme $Z$.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 01YL, third paragraph, the implicit use that a nonzero ideal on integral $Z_0$ is nonzero at its generic point

proof.text: If (b) holds, then $\mathcal I$ has a nonzero section and is not the zero sheaf, giving (a). Conversely, if $\mathcal I\ne0$, there is an open $V$ and a section $s\in\mathcal I(V)$ which is not zero. Its germ is nonzero at some point $z\in V$, since a section whose germs all vanish is zero by the sheaf axiom [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Choose a nonempty affine open $U\subseteq V$ containing $z$; the restriction $s|_U$ has the same nonzero germ, so $\mathcal I(U)\ne0$. Step 2 then gives (d), and thus (b). This proves (a), (b), and (d) equivalent.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 01YL, third paragraph, the unstated implication from a nonzero ideal sheaf to a nonzero generic stalk

proof.text: The stalk $\mathcal I_\eta$ is an ideal of the field $\mathcal O_{Z,\eta}$, as stated, and a field has exactly two ideals: if an ideal contains $0\ne a$, it contains $a^{-1}a=1$ and is the whole field. Thus (c) and (d) are equivalent. With step 3 this gives all four equivalences and the field assertion.
